$comment: The AndroidX samples pin for :samples-catalog. See docs/design/ANDROIDX_SAMPLES.md. One entry per LIBRARY, because a sample tree belongs to the artifact whose KDoc points at it: each carries its own `ref` (a COMMIT SHA, never a branch, so a render is reproducible and an upstream bump is a reviewable diff) and its own `artifactVersion` — the AndroidX version whose @sample set matches the Compose Multiplatform artifact this repo compiles against. Derived, not guessed, and re-derived by scripts/samples-drift.mjs on every run: when a CMP artifact moves, the check fails and names the version to bump to, per library. `composeMultiplatformVersionRef` is the gradle/libs.versions.toml key holding the CMP version to compare against, because the two libraries here move on independent cadences. `paths` are subtrees of the upstream repository, fetched with a blobless sparse clone (13 MB, not the multi-GB whole tree).

libraries.name: material3
libraries.refDescription: androidx-main as of 2026-06-17, the day material3 1.5.0-alpha22 was published — the version whose @sample set matches the Compose Multiplatform artifact this repo compiles against. Derived, not chosen: the androidx GitHub mirror publishes no tags, so the commit is resolved by date from the artifact POM's Last-Modified, and scripts/samples-drift.mjs re-derives the VERSION half on every run.

libraries.name: material3-adaptive
libraries.refDescription: androidx-main as of 2026-05-19, the day adaptive-layout 1.3.0-beta02 was published, resolved by the same Last-Modified rule as material3's. A SEPARATE ref, and that is the reason this manifest holds a list rather than one pin: the adaptive line moves on its own cadence, and material3's commit is three weeks later on it. Vendoring the adaptive samples at material3's ref compiles them against a newer adaptive API than Compose Multiplatform ships — measured, not feared: `AnimatedPane(shape = …)` at that commit against a CMP 1.3.0-beta02 `AnimatedPane` with no `shape` parameter.
